## Consultant delivery acceptance check

**Reconstruct the evidence**

- A reviewer can trace the objective to the selected workflow, human-authored DoD, source evidence, tests, result and named decision.

- Permissions match actual users, data, tools and degree of autonomy. Task risk, operating tier and legal classification remain separate.

- All attempted cases, refusals, corrections and fallback work are represented. Raw observations reconcile to summary totals; setup effort is separate.

- Control effectiveness is supported by tests. Provided evidence is not described as verified. Unknowns have owners, deadlines and scope restrictions.

- Every Tier 3 service released in the engagement has a Service Record on file, and Tier 2 records are present where the owner chose to write them.

**Confirm the transfer**

- The receiver can operate the review cycle, retrieve the evidence, use fallback, escalate an incident and trigger reauthorization.

- Open actions have resources, deadlines and closure tests. The Client has a signed recommendation and a continuing plan.

**Deliverables accepted and exceptions**

Record any missing deliverable, remedy, responsible party and due date. Commercial acceptance does not authorize production use.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

This check closes the consulting delivery. W23 records the organizational use decision. W13 records acceptance of each work product.
